paragraphs.text: . This whole chapter is but a preface to the ensuing prophecy, or visional prediction, recorded in the two following chapters. It beginneth at the third year of Cyrus’s empire, and reacheth till the time of the Jews rising from the dust of their dispersion, say some; to the end of the world, say others, with whom I concur.
paragraphs.anchor: In the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia.

paragraphs.text: Who now must needs be very old, yet at those years (a hundred or more) gave himself to understand and search into divine secrets. The more any one knoweth of God, the more he would still know. Moses, newly come from the mount, crieth to God to show him his glory. David, that gulf of holy learning, is often at his, Teach me thy statutes, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: A thing was revealed unto Daniel.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Plain and proper; not, as former visions, figurative and obscure.
paragraphs.anchor: And the thing was true

paragraphs.text: scil., Till all be fulfilled, which will not be till the last judgment.
paragraphs.anchor: But the time appointed was long

paragraphs.text: And so was the better able to propound it to the Church; for what a man doth not himself understand, he cannot well and fitly deliver to others.
paragraphs.anchor: And he understood the thing.

paragraphs.text: scil., Given unto him; for unless God give us both sight and light, we perceive not heavenly doctrine, neither indeed can do.
paragraphs.anchor: And had understood the vision

paragraphs.text: Though a great man still, and in great account, yet not now so great at court as to hinder and defeat the malicious designs of Cambyses’s counsellors; who, being bribed by the Jews’ adversaries, put a stop to the temple work at Jerusalem. {Ezr 4:1-4} This disaster cast good Daniel into his dumps, so that he fasted three full weeks, a tanto et tali, sed non a toto, and longer might, had not the angel taken him off by an answer of peace. {Dan 10:12} Abstinet ab omni cura cultuque corporis, sua sponte. See the like, 1Sa 31:13.
paragraphs.anchor: In those days I Daniel was mourning.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Weeks of days, to distinguish them from those seventy weeks of years. {Dan 9:24}
paragraphs.anchor: Three full weeks.

paragraphs.text: Bread he ate, for animantis cuiusque vita in fuga est, life will fail if not maintained by food, but coarse bread panem cibarium, atrum, et siligineum, and no more of that either than needs must. He voluntarily abridged himself of lawful delights, macerating and mortifying his flesh, that he might communicate with his poor afflicted brethren, and pray the harder for them. Fasting inflameth prayer, and prayer sanctifieth fasting.
paragraphs.anchor: I ate no pleasant bread.

paragraphs.text: All delights of sense must be laid aside in a time of solemn humiliation, but yet without annoyance and uncomeliness, as music, mirth, perfumes, brave apparel; {2Sa 12:20 Joh 3:8 Exo 33:4-6 1Ki 21:27} cheerfulness, outward joy, and pleasure (Mar 2:20 Luk 5:35 cf. Mat 9:15 Jdg 20:26 1Sa 7:6). It is spoken of as a foul sin; Isa 58:3, "Behold in the day of your fast ye find pleasure."
paragraphs.anchor: Neither did I anoint myself at all.

paragraphs.text: The day is thus noted, because the matters here revealed were most memorable.
paragraphs.anchor: And on the four and twentieth of the first month.

paragraphs.text: Meditating likely, because the city was full of noise and tumult, and praying. {as Act 16:13} Broughton giveth this reason, because Seleucus Nicator, founder of the Seleucidae, much spoken of in the ensuing vision, built his chief city upon this river.
paragraphs.anchor: As I was by the side of the great river.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Sharp swift; called also Tigris, from the swiftest of all beasts, the tiger; but Curtius and Pliny {a} say, that Tigris in the Median language signifieth an arrow. Here Daniel was personally present, and not visionally only. See Dan 10:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Which is Hiddekel

paragraphs.text: {a} Plin, lib. vi. cap. 7.

viz., After my long fasting, praying, and meditating. So Moses and Elias, those great fasters, met together with our Saviour gloriously in the mount at his transfiguration. It is abstinence, not fulness, that makes a man capable of heavenly visions of divine glory.
paragraphs.anchor: Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked

paragraphs.text: Heb., One man; a singular man, a glorious person; Messias the prince, described here by his habit and parts as a judge, say some, or as a priest, say others. See Dan 12:6-7 Rev 1:13-15; Rev 10:5.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold a certain man.

paragraphs.text: To show his innocence and purity, as also his righteousnesses, imputed and imparted, wherewith he clotheth his saints, {Rev 19:8} that fine white linen and shining.
paragraphs.anchor: Clothed in linen.

paragraphs.text: Or, Of Ophir; Peru, haply, or Malaca, or Sopbala. This golden girdle about his loins denoteth Christ’s strength and alacrity. {Psa 93:1 Luk 17:8}
paragraphs.anchor: Whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz.

paragraphs.text: Of an azure colour, like the heavens. The "second Adam is the Lord from heaven." {1Co 15:47} Some render it the chrysolite, which is of the colour of the sea; to note, say they, his power to purge the Church by his Word, Spirit, and judgments, as by the water of the sea.
paragraphs.anchor: His body also was like the beryl.

paragraphs.text: Which both shineth and terrifieth, and soon appeareth from the one end of the heaven to the other; {Mat 24:27} Christ suddenly discovereth all things though never so remote. {Psa 90:8 Eze 1:13}
paragraphs.anchor: And his face as the appearance of lightning.

paragraphs.text: To note his omniscience, his wrath also and readiness to revenge. {Jer 32:19}
paragraphs.anchor: And his eyes as lamps of fire.

paragraphs.text: Scintillantes purissime. To note his omnipotence in the execution of his wrath while he trampleth on his enemies, as he that hath brazen arms and feet cart easily break in pieces a potter’s vessel.
paragraphs.anchor: And his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass.

paragraphs.text: Strepitus - i.e., Maris. Or, As the noise of many waters, {Rev 1:15} noting the efficacy of Christ’s doctrine. See Act 2:4.
paragraphs.anchor: And the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.

paragraphs.text: Holy prophets alone are capable of holy visions. {2Pe 1:19}
paragraphs.anchor: And I Daniel alone saw the vision.

paragraphs.text: Sensible they were of some alteration upon the waters, and somewhat wrought upon; not for their information, but separation from Daniel, that he might more freely undergo the heavenly rapture. See the like, Act 9:7.
paragraphs.anchor: For the men that were with me saw not.

paragraphs.text: Through sense of sin and fear of wrath. This served to show the truth of the vision.
paragraphs.anchor: But a great quaking fell upon them.

paragraphs.text: Daniel, though much frightened, keepeth his station, when the rest fled and hid themselves. Good is the counsel of the apostle, Heb 12:13, "Make straight steps unto your feet, lest that which is halting be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed."
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore I was left alone.

paragraphs.text: See Dan 7:15; Dan 7:28; Dan 8:27.
paragraphs.anchor: For my comeliness, &c.

paragraphs.text: What these words were is not here expressed; but by comparing, they may be gathered to be the same with those, Dan 8:18, bidding Gabriel to draw near and speak unto the prophet.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet heard I the voice of his words.

paragraphs.text: See Dan 8:18. The more the outward man is bound, the fitter he is for holy communion with God. {2Co 12:2-3}
paragraphs.anchor: Then was I in a deep sleep.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The hand of the angel Gabriel, who was sent by Christ to dictate unto Daniel the prophecy following. It is Christ’s use to signify prophecies by his angel, {Rev 1:1-2} and this angel is accordingly strengthened by Michael {Dan 10:21} - that is, by Christ.
paragraphs.anchor: And, behold, an hand touched me

paragraphs.text: In a praying posture; but yet he continued trembling, {Dan 10:11} and was not raised and restored but by certain degrees, the better to frame and fit him to a religious attention and docility.
paragraphs.anchor: Which set me upon my knees.

paragraphs.text: Such shall know God’s secrets. {Pro 3:32} See Dan 9:23.
paragraphs.anchor: O Daniel, a man greatly beloved.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Stand upon thy standing. God by his grace and Word will raise up those that humble themselves in his presence.
paragraphs.anchor: Stand upright.

paragraphs.text: “ Deiecit ut relevet. ”
Disquieting and expectorating fears should be laid aside. {1Jn 4:18}
paragraphs.anchor: Fear not, Daniel.

paragraphs.text: See on Dan 9:23. Let us but find a praying heart, and God will presently find a pitying heart, though he may delay for a season to send in an answer. Though Daniel heard nothing of his prayers for three weeks’ time, yet was the angel at work all that while for the removal of impediments. Daniel in the meanwhile wrought hard with God, as it is elsewhere said of Jonathan. {1Sa 14:45}
paragraphs.anchor: For from the first day.

paragraphs.text: Brought hither by thy prayers. God will come, but he will have his people’s prayers lead him into the field as it were.
paragraphs.anchor: And I am come for thy word.

paragraphs.text: By this prince of Persia some understand wicked Cambyses. Others, {a} an evil angel, that by his suggestions swayed Cambyses to oppose and retard the rebuilding of the temple. There is a principal devil, prince of this world; and there are, as some hold, princes or principal spirits in countries and nations under him. {Eph 6:12}
paragraphs.anchor: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Christ the Lord of angels, head of the Church. {Dan 12:1-13: 1Ki 12:7} By these chief princes may be understood the three persons in trinity, or the created angels. The Septuagint translate the word ευσθυμουντων, the cheerful ones, who serve the Lord readily, freely, and joyfully in his wars; making Zion as dreadful to all her enemies, {Psa 68:17} as those angels once made Sinai, at the delivery of the law.
paragraphs.anchor: But, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes

paragraphs.text: With Cambyses and his counsellors, to repress their rage, and to blast their designs against the Church; which, when it is opposed, the holy angels interpose. {Psa 34:7}
paragraphs.anchor: And I remained there with the kings of Persia.

paragraphs.text: {a} Melanchthon, Osiander, Pappus.
As it were with weariness of flight. {as Dan 9:21} Comfort will come at length. {Heb 10:37}
paragraphs.anchor: Now I am come.

paragraphs.text: Toward the end of their state, and not long before the coming of the Messiah, who shall begin another age, and as it were a new world. {Eze 38:8 Heb 2:3}
paragraphs.anchor: In the latter days.

paragraphs.text: Coharrui totus, et vex faucibus haesit. See how deeply God’s darlings are again affected at the hearing of his holy Word. {Hab 3:16}
paragraphs.anchor: I set my face toward the ground, and I became dumb.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The angel in human shape. {as Dan 10:10}
paragraphs.anchor: And, behold, one like the similitude

paragraphs.text: Restored unto me my speech. Good affections wanting expression shall have God’s furtherance.
paragraphs.anchor: Touched my lips.

paragraphs.text: i.e., To Christ, whom he had seen. {Dan 10:5-6}
paragraphs.anchor: And said unto him that stood before me

paragraphs.text: Heb., My bowels, which are even strained and straitened.
paragraphs.anchor: My sorrows are turned upon me.

paragraphs.text: It is ordinary with God’s people in their prayers to complain much of their own weakness. {Jer 31:18}
paragraphs.anchor: And I have retained no strength.

paragraphs.text: . Qui tantulus sum, et tam imbecillis. God’s praying servants use to speak as broken men. They well understand, (1.) Their distance; (2.) Dependence.
paragraphs.anchor: For how can the servant of this my lord.

paragraphs.text: Prayer is a holy interparlance with the divine Majesty: εντευξις. {1Ti 2:1}
paragraphs.anchor: Talk with this my lord.

paragraphs.text: I am hardly able to bear up or breathe. Human frailty cannot endure God’s presence without fainting. {Rev 1:17}
paragraphs.anchor: Neither is there breath in me.

paragraphs.text: Not all at once, but by four degrees, was Daniel raised: (1.) He is set upon his knees and palms of his hands, {Dan 10:10} an emblem of prayer; (2.) He is caused to stand upon his feet, though trembling and silent; {Dan 10:11; Dan 10:15} (3.) His mouth is opened to speak, though not without much weakness, fears, and sorrows; {Dan 10:17} (4.) He is fully strengthened here. God loves to hold his praying people long in request. He is also "a God of judgment" - one that well understandeth when and how to bestow his favours; "Blessed are all they that wait for him." {Isa 30:18}
paragraphs.anchor: Then there came again and touched me.

paragraphs.text: Holy angels are ready to strengthen such as are ready to faint in holy duties.
paragraphs.anchor: Be strong, yea, be strong.

paragraphs.text: q.d., I told thee that before, {Dan 10:14} and I look thou shouldst remember it.
paragraphs.anchor: Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee?

paragraphs.text: To defeat and prevent his tyranny and cruel intents against thy people, {see Dan 10:13} not without the devil’s hand and help.
paragraphs.anchor: I will return to fight with the prince of Persia.

paragraphs.text: sc., Out of Persia.
paragraphs.anchor: And when I am gone forth

paragraphs.text: Great Alexander, whom I will fetch in, so that the Persians shall have henceforth little leisure or mind to meddle with the Jews. There were other Grecian captains also before Alexander, who found the Persians somewhat to do, as Leonidas, Miltiades, Themistocles; but he overturned their monarchy.
paragraphs.anchor: Lo, the prince of Grecia.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In God’s infallible and unchangeable decree, which, for our apprehension, are here compared to court rolls and records, ex usu forensi. And God’s providence, which is nothing else but the carrying on of his decree, is that helm which turneth about the whole ship of the universe.
paragraphs.anchor: In the scripture of truth

paragraphs.text: And there is none … but Michael your prince.] But how many reckon we him at? as that king once said of himself to his fearful soldiers. He alone is a whole army of men, van and rear both. {Isa 52:12}
